title: Run of the loop-body machine
statement: Let $B$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and let $x$ be a Boolean input. Let $c$ be a configuration of $B$ on $x$ whose state is present, let $r$ be a Boolean, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every $u<t$, the configuration reached from $c$ after $u$ steps has a present state, and that its state is not $a$ except possibly when $u=0$ and $r$ is true. Then after $t$ steps, the machine formed by adding one work tape and a Boolean release flag to the control state has the configuration obtained from the base machine's configuration after $t$ steps: the release flag is $r$ if $t=0$ and false otherwise, and the added tape has true at cell zero exactly when the base machine has halted by time $t$, and is blank there otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine over Booleans
An initial configuration of the base machine
The initial configuration has a present state
The base run has a present state at every time $u<t$
At times $u<t$, the state avoids the anchor unless $u=0$ and release is true
